title: Light up your space with glowing houseplants - Nature Biotechnology
text:
Magicpen’s genetically engineered plants have a heightened bioluminescence. While most traditional plant engineering uses the phenylalanine metabolism pathway, which requires five or six genes working in a coordinated way, the startup developed an efficient dual-gene system. The TAL tyrosine pathway enables the plants to emit light continuously because it introduces both a gene from fireflies to produce the luciferase enzyme needed to oxidize the substrate luciferin to produce visible light and genes from luminous fungi to produce the enzymes needed for the luminescent substrate. A small peptide tag in the coding sequence of the luciferase enzyme blocks degradative enzymes and increases the glow’s half-life.“It took several years and over 500 iterations to achieve our current high brightness level,” says Li.
